summary: The base reproduces the reported AITER/ROCm ordering defect. At the exact candidate commit, requested FP4 expert dequantization runs before the native AITER FP4 early return and before FNUZ handling. Focused regressions and an independent real-GPU AITER post-load exercise pass.

tests.what_was_measured: Issue-specific failing-before behavior: both FNUZ parameterizations entered AITER FP4 preparation without invoking the requested conversion; two boundary cases passed. See raw/base_candidate_test.log.
Eleven focused tests passed, covering AITER with FNUZ on/off, flag-off and non-FP4 boundaries, and related block-FP8/DeepGEMM processing. See raw/candidate_focused.log.

tests.command: SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-3bf9b5c3bab6/venv/bin/python <independent inline GPU post-load exercise> (at candidate commit)
tests.what_was_measured: On one gfx950 GPU, real packed FP4 tensors were converted and real AITER shuffle/normalization completed for FNUZ false and true; is_fp4_expert became false and output shapes/dtypes were valid. See raw/candidate_gpu_method_aiter.log.

gpu_execution.evidence: raw/candidate_gpu_method_aiter.log records AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, and successful real AITER post-load processing for both FNUZ branches.

remaining_limitations: The available hardware was one gfx950 MI350X rather than the reported eight gfx942 MI308X GPUs.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 weights were unavailable, so full server startup, graph capture, GSM8K, TP8, multi-rank dispatch, and multi-node behavior remain unverified.
The gfx942-relevant FNUZ control path was forced on gfx950 for branch validation; it was not executed on physical gfx942 hardware.
No native source changed, so native rebuilding was not applicable.
The candidate PR body cites https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/1433 instead of the requested mirror issue https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/1493.
